quest.title: Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4, Unknown Item #364506 x1

chapter.title: Blue Longing of Heart and Moon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what's wrong? Why can't we continue on?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Strange... it seems like something's blocking the way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, what do we do...

choices.text: We could use Seymour to break the wall down...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: #I apologize, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.}{NICKNAME}, but that is impossible. The thickness of the rock wall exceeds my output limits. I would run out of energy before a tunnel could be successfully bored.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: S—Swim... from over there... Father's... blood... is already...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Blood? Mamere, are you okay? What blood?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: We cannot... delay any further. Let's swim from over there...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: That's right. Swim... Over there... Because Father's blood... is already...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Blood? Mamere, are you okay? What blood?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: We cannot... delay any further. Let's swim from over there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! What happened to that strange giant stone all of a sudden!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And look at that color! Doesn't it basically look like a heart?
That's right. This is the original form of the "heart."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait. That's... you're Jakob!

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: What are you... doing...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Gathering "paint," as you can see.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Hah. "Paint." What an interesting way to describe this filth — and to think that anyone would set it upon canvas...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Wh—What...!?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Still, your arrival here was quite unexpected.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I could've sworn I sealed all the entrances — did I slip up somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You're a member of the Abyss Order, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh! Where there's smoke, there's fire — and where there's evil, there's you guys, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The Abyss Order? Oh, please, do not lump me in with those benighted primitives.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: They are no different from those oppressors — the power they seek is but a tool that only a few can use. What we search for is true equality. The liberation of the will.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Just as my friend said, those who lack weakness of consciousness shall not be subdued either by gods or death.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stop your prattling! If you aren't with the Abyss Order, how do you explain the magic you used earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I merely used the power of the Abyss to reverse the crystallization process. That's all.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: In any case, I had not expected to see its heart withered to such an extent after a mere few hundred years. As such, it needed to be restarted for me to obtain sufficient blood.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sufficient blood?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Yes. A rather inelegant method of doing things, you might think.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Alas, there is no other way. I, too, initially believed that I could obtain enough congealed blood from Ms. Mamere through peaceful means.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: This would've allowed the plan to go through without alerting the Marechaussee Hunters. Alas, that backfired. Too bad, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, didn't you previously say that you wanted paint? What's this congealed blood you're blabbering about?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Explain.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Wait a moment... Hah, this is more interesting than I thought. So you don't actually know what those paints really are, or the power they contain?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I see, I see... it seems I spoke too much — how terribly unexpected.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Still, I fail to understand — why would you want to get close to Ms. Mamere, if you don't understand the value of those "paints"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Don't bring us down to the level of sneaky scheming schemers like yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Besides, you summoned the monsters earlier, didn't you? What did you do that for? Why did you have to attack the other Melusines?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Attack them? I hardly have the time for such frivolous pursuits.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Well, in theory, the arrays I activated in those ruins to reverse the crystallization would indeed have temporarily opened the way into the realm of beasts...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I suppose that's how the monsters you mentioned were attracted here — like flies to festering meat on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: As for those Melusines... Well. An unrelated matter, I fear. Let's not discuss them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: #Compared to that, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, do indulge my curiosity. What do you think of the original sights here, now that you've seen them?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Look at your feet. Blood, flowing like a river, fertilizing the very dust of the earth with their filthy fat.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: If I told you that a greater disaster than that will come one day, how would you react?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what are you talking about? Blood, fat... Hasn't this place only turned just a little bit red?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Negative. The blood has already risen over {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}'s ankles. The local contamination index is now over ten times the human body's endurance threshold.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I recommend that all present leave this area for your own safety and to prevent the following: allergies, confusion, white matter distortion, mental deterioration, and...

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I see. That's how far it's gone, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: How sad. But fear not. I will liberate you.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The moment foretold by the "world-formula" is coming. There is little time left.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: #Is there anything else you'd like to talk about, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Fascinating. I'd thought that you were only able to reach this place purely through luck — but it appears as if that was not all.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: #Indulge my curiosity, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}. Could you tell me who you are... exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's none of your concern.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Not going to answer? Well, that's fine. It was just a mild curiosity of mine, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: In any case, I haven't any further time to waste here.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: The appointed time is coming, and I have enough blood to use. Any further delay may invite unwanted attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're not gonna let you get away! What "time" are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: And that is none of your concern. It has nothing to do with you, after all. Anyway—

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}...? Look out!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What the...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wh—What is this? You despicable... What have you done to {NICKNAME}!?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: I wouldn't use that word. This is a matter of utility, not morality.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: #You are indeed very strong, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, but I wouldn't say the same for the others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh! Where did these monsters come from this time!?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Apologies, Jakob Ingold, but I fear I cannot let you do this.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Ms. Mamere, Ms. Paimon, please get behind me. My duty is to defend. All attempts to harm you will not succeed.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Such arrogance, you piece of soulless scrap.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: You were unable to defend Mary-Ann then — all you will do today is confront that incompetence once more.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Mary... Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: ...And should you survive this battle, the giant revived beast will crush and digest you all.

dialogues.speaker: Jakob
dialogues.text: Well then, farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh, they're coming this way!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. Ms. Mary-Ann was my master, and my prime directive was to accompany her on *garbled mechanical noises* behalf and ensure that she would smile happily.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I have not been able to fulfill that duty for (1/7)×10^21 clockwork cycles due to the lack of a relay module.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: In truth, I cannot ascertain Ms. Mary-Ann's present location, either. This should never happen. My logic unit requires immediate repair.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: As such, if you do not mind, allow me to depart for now. My standard deduction module has already calculated the most likely location where I may collect information, and I must go there.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Eh? Wait, Seymour. Are you leaving...?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative. I thank you for your care thus far, Ms. Mamere, but I have a duty that I must fulfill.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Th—Then I'll come too...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Negative. Deduced danger level: High. For your safety, I must refuse your proposal, Ms. Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: But I will promise to return and express formal gratitude to you once I find my master.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, some of my memories remain damaged, so I do not presently know where the Narzissenkreuz Ordo that I must reach is, precisely.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: As such, my search will inevitably take a great deal of time. For that, you have my apologies in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: I see... I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: There's something you must do, and so you have to leave. But you'll come back to find me, won't you, Seymour?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Affirmative.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Alright, then. Be careful, Seymour...

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: You have to come back, alright. My token, the symbol of my life, is with you, so don't go breaking down someplace where I can't find you...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: You have my word, Ms. Mamere. I will fulfill my mission and return to your spatial coordinates.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: O—Okay, got it, got it! A—Anyway, I've suddenly got a bout of inspiration, so I'm going to go paint now. Don't forget to come back and see me when you've finished your work, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You have a deal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll take care of Seymour for you for now.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #Alright, I understand! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, Seymour, you all stay safe, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: I'll... make a move first...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mamere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, uh, where are we going next? Seymour mentioned this place called the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Narzissenkreuz Ordo?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... What sorta place is the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Searching... Insufficient data. Unable to answer.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My standard deduction module was only able to give this name. Apart from that, I do not possess any related information.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, then how are we supposed to find the place!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can help.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Calculating... Affirmative. Your presence on the journey will greatly increase its success rate.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: #Thank you very much for your help, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But let's just go anyway! Once everything's settled, we'll bring you back to see Mamere!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about your origins...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Sure! My mother is the reason I exist. Mother is the most wonderful person in this world. She gave me my name — and it is a lovely name.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Before I was born, I floated in the cosmic darkness. It was cold there, and lonely. I was so sad, then, and I would often cry.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: But later, I heard Mother's voice.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: She wished for me to be born into a beautiful world, to give me life, to give me a strong and healthy body that could walk the world, to grant me a beautiful name.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: She wanted to give me many siblings, wanted me to meet many friends, wanted me to see the beautiful sights beyond that cosmic dark.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: She did not deceive me, and I was very happy. My elder siblings treated me well, and later, many younger ones came along — and I treated them just as my elder siblings treated me.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Later, we left the world beneath the earth. I felt the wind brushing against my skin, the warmth of the sun, waters icy and warm.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Life is wonderful — and it was wonderful that I was able to witness this world!

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Only later did I discover that I was different from the life in this world. The things that brought me happiness, the things that interested me... they were frightening and terribly hurtful to those of this world.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Eventually, I fell here and died. That saddened yet gladdened me. I treasured the life I was given by Mother, but my life would bring everyone such pain... so it was better this way.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Later, just as Mother gave me life, I gave my children life, that they may walk upon this world — that makes me very proud and very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Jakob...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: That person from before, you mean? I fear I know little about him. He is not like you — even after drinking my blood, he cannot speak to me as you do.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: In the beginning, he came with someone else to search for the blood within my body. At that time, I could feel that they were different.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: There is something within him — a bit of the dark, cold cosmos's power.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: And aha, I thought, so my blood will do him good — wonderful!

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Later, he would come often to collect my blood, all the way up till there was a great battle involving many people here, him included. He didn't come back again after that.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: To be honest, I was worried that he might have died. Imagine how happy I was to see him return — alive and well, and so tall and strong!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, guess we're finally safe, huh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, what was with that round thing? It was... helping us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mamere, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: ...Yes, Father.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Eh? Here...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: O—Oh. Paimon thought you were talking to us...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's that sound again...)

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: ...I understand. Since this is your will, it will be done.

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... Could you both strike a pose? I'm going to start drawing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Wait a moment! Paimon hasn't mentally prepared herself, or figured out what pose to strike— actually, wait. Why are we doing this here and now!?

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Um... I don't know how to explain, but I think Seymour can help...

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Logic module... calculating... Attempting to rationalize reason for question. Results: Insufficient data. Cannot answer.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My logic module concludes that your decision is far from logical, Ms. Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously, Seymour, what are you doing... and also, why did you push the problem to him, Mamere?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: My primary design goal is to... Now sorting data fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Seymour? You okay? Oh boy, looks like he's "hanged."

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: Sorry, Paimon, but there's no more time to explain. If we don't hurry, it'll be too late.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, sure, okay. This doesn't quite feel right, but Paimon trusts you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have faith in you too, Mamere.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I know you won't do anything to harm us on purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... Ugh, Paimon hasn't decided what pose to strike yet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Any thoughts, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: (Strike an "all goes just as planned" pose.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, Paimon'll also—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What do you think? Will holding this pose do?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Yup, you look great.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Now then, leave the rest to me.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Mamere takes a deep breath, almost as if encouraging herself, and with a few wags of her short little tail, she gets to work without another word. Her expression and the looks she gives you are resolute and earnest — solemn, some might even say.\nNot long after, her work is done.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: It's... done.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that was super quick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, let's have a look, shall we...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that's right, there's nowhere to run now! Uh... Where's Paimon supposed to stand, though?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, yup, that's the kind of confidence you should have in a situation like this—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About that Breacher Primus from earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Ah! Well, I saw that you were trapped and thought, "If this goes on, I will be revived, and you will all die."

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: My strength began to return, and so I thought, why don't I use one of my cells to attack the thing trapping you? That way, you'd be able to move.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That was one of your cells?

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: That's right! They can help to drive harmful things away from my body and protect my children. However, they aren't as smart as my children, so they will attack you too. Sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Still, I'm glad to have helped out!

talks.objective: Use the prism to resonate with the ores

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I need to go. Paimon and Mamere will worry.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Well, I'm almost out of time, too! There are a lot of things I'd love to talk to you about, but the life I received this time is almost spent.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: #Could you do me a favor, though, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Could you tell Mamere... Hmm, what to say...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: How about this, then? "Your paintings are very beautiful. I love you, and I'm so very proud of you."

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Ah, right, and "please get along with your sisters — they love you very much as well."

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: #Thanks a bunch, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've got it.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Alright then, thank you! Honestly, it was great meeting you. Someday, I hope that I'll be able to traverse this world without fear of causing harm or death to others.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: When that time comes, I'll be sure to show you what I really look like!

talks.objective: Meet the owner of the voice

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Mary-Ann? That Jakob guy mentioned that name as well, didn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Paimon's sure she's heard that name somewhere...
#Ah, you're finally here. I've always wanted to meet you and talk to you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know me?
Yes. I've been watching you all this time... Or should I say "sensing" you? I felt your presence ever since that child of mine who loves art brought you inside my body.
It was like a warm light was running to and fro within my organs and blood vessels.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Elynas...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Yes. That's my name. Beautiful, isn't it? I love it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why did you appear in the form of a Melusine?

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: #Why? Well, I find that form to be very beautiful. Don't you think so too, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: I love them very much, for they are, one and all, my lovely children. In here, I can decide my own appearance, so of course, I chose the look I love the most.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Melusine are your children?

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: That's right! That happened a long, long time ago. Not long after I first experienced death, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Many, many people, a spirit of the primordial waters, and many metal animals came into my body.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: I thought that they, like those two other people, were here to explore and gather my blood. I was originally just happy to have people here, but they chose to fight each other in the end instead.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: But of course, I was dead at that point. I was too weak to do anything beyond watching them in silence and feeling the wounds they left inside my body.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: In the end, someone triggered an explosion that caused a terrible shockwave. Many people died, and those metal animals also died. The survivors left, and everything was very quiet once more.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: A lot of sharp shards pierced my body from the explosion's impact, but later, tiny life emerged from those wounds and from my broken flesh.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: I was so overjoyed, for they were beautiful and intelligent. Also, that was when I realized that I could do more than destroy — I could bring beautiful new life into this world.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: So I spoke to them, and I told them of many things. I taught them how to build a home for themselves so that they might grow up well. Then, there was happiness and liveliness everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Later, they gradually became unable to hear my voice. That's fine, though — just as Mother once said farewell to me, all children must grow up and leave their parents.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Only that child who loves painting still speaks to me, and she even brought her friends — that's how I came to meet you. I truly am happy that that's the case.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're Mamere's "Father"...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: That's right!

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Still, you truly are special. It was only when the situation was past salvaging that I realized how my blood was poisonous to humans.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: But when you came into contact with my blood, not only did you not get poisoned, but instead, you slowly became linked to my and my daughters' consciousnesses — you began to see and sense many things.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: You are the second person I have met who did not fear my blood. Ah, if only there were more people like you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who was the other person?

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Ah, so you don't know each other? But I saw you saying so many things to one another. I refer to the person who made my heart start beating again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jakob...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: A long, long time ago, he and someone else came into my body to collect my blood. Absorbing my blood would really raise his spirits!

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: At that time, my children were not yet born, and I felt rather lonely as I lay here. As such, I was very pleased to meet them — and I was very pleased to have helped him out.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: He must've tried to restart my heart to thank me for helping him out using my blood...

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: But I'm afraid I can't accept his kindness. As such, I thank you for stopping him — and me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: Well, if I were to be revived, my heart would beat, my blood would surge, and my internal organs would come to life again.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: What would happen to my children then? They and their beautiful little houses would be crushed and digested. That would be too terrible a tragedy.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: I might look like this now, but my body is, in truth, very big and frightening.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: In the beginning, my siblings and I took leave of our Mother and came to play on the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: But I realized at last that the things I found fun and joyous were terrifying to others. It was too late by then — and I was filled with grief and regret.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: That's why I asked Mamere to use my blood to create a painting and give it to you. That way, I'd get the chance to thank you in person.

dialogues.speaker: Elynas
dialogues.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}, for stopping my heart. So long as I live, I will bring grief to others, and I never wish to see that happen ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're very welcome.

choices.text: I mean, I did it to survive, too.

response.speaker: Elynas
response.text: I see. Anyway, this is a rare opportunity. I haven't been this clear-minded in a very long time. Why don't we chat about some other things?

choices.text: I did it to stop Jakob as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! {NICKNAME}! Are you alright? You've been staring at that painting this whole time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously, you were just like Seymour... He just said he would be "searching for data," and since then, he's just... not moved at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Your paintings are very beautiful."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "I love you, and I'm so very proud of you."

dialogues.speaker: Mamere
dialogues.text: #Eh? {NICKNAME}, you... I... You...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait just a minute, where did all that come from? Are you okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Someone asked me to pass their words on to you, Mamere.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I see. Thank you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Please get along with your sisters."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "They love you very much as well."

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I— Come on, I've always gotten along well with everyone. Seriously...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #But since Father said so... I got it. Thank you, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Paimon didn't notice this before, but when did that thing over there turn back to stone? The shaking from before seems to be stopped, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. Were you in such a hurry to paint for us because...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait, Paimon's got it! People call really good paintings "absorbing," don't they? So you painted that in order to "absorb" {NICKNAME}, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Hmm, no, that doesn't make sense — what happened, really?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll explain in detail later.

choices.text: The problem here seems to have been resolved, at least.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. Alright then, but you'd better explain later!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: #Yes. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, what do you think of this painting? Um, well, please feel free to critique it...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I didn't have much time, and I wasn't my best self, so I'm not very confident about it...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Ah, that feels like an excuse! I've got to stop doing that!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: So... What do you think...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—Which part of it do you like? Paimon can't understand it at all...

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: That's... wonderful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't know what to say about your art other than "it looks amazing"... Huh. Is this what they'd call an "artistic baptism of fire"?

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: Well, I'm glad you like it either way. As long as you do, I'm happy.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: I'm not a very good speaker, unlike you, Paimon. But when I'm with you, I'm very happy. That's why I want to give you something that makes you happy, too...

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Preliminary memory fragment sorting is complete.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! You're back, Seymour!

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I may now answer previously unanswerable questions as well.

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: "Previously unanswerable"... Which questions were those?

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: The one about my "master" that Ms. Paimon asked, as well as my aforementioned "purpose."

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: I am Prototype 4ACV07, designed by *garbled mechanical noises* to accompany and protect my master, Ms. Mary-Ann.

choices.text: It's even cooler than the real Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What? Paimon doesn't get the painting at all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon's not great with words. But... Um...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME} sure looks like {M#he}{F#she} loves it! Look, {M#he's}{F#she's} practically speechless!

response.speaker: Mamere
response.text: ...What? Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Of course. Paimon's been {NICKNAME}'s travel companion for a long, long time. We've got a real "tacit understanding" thing going on, y'know!

choices.text: We're safe for now — us and the Melusines.
My eyes are a little dry from all that staring.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I know where to find the place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon thinks we've already been there... The way in is pretty mysterious, though. Paimon wonders if you'll be able to get in there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But let's just go anyway! Once everything's settled, we'll bring you back to see Mamere!
